title: Number of Bit Changes to Make Two Integers Equal
summary: Given two positive integers n and k, determine the count of bit changes required to convert n into k by flipping any number of 1s in n to 0s.
statement: Given two positive integers n and k, determine the count of bit changes required to convert n into k by flipping any number of 1s in n to 0s. If conversion is impossible, return -1.
constraints: In one operation, change a set bit of n from one to zero.
Bits cannot change from zero to one.
Return the minimum operations needed to reach k, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Every one bit required by k must already be set in n.
Test this subset condition with n&k==k.
When possible, differing bits are precisely extra one bits of n; count them in n XOR k.
Each extra bit requires one operation independently, proving the count minimal.
editorial: Each extra bit requires one operation independently, proving the count minimal.

tests.explanation: Binary 1101 becomes 0100 by clearing two set bits.
The values already match, so zero changes are needed.
